scope: All 152 managed NourishPlan recipes and their rendering surfaces
method: All 44 original shared photographs were visually inspected. Original source PDF photos were checked against the current normalized recipes. Mismatches were replaced with recipe-specific generated illustrations using the actual ingredients and preparation methods. Every generated cell was visually reviewed in reading order for its main protein, carbohydrate, prepared form and sides. A targeted correction on atlas 02 removed unlisted sesame-like garnish from chicken adobo.
quantityNote: Illustrated portions and counts are not measurement guides; follow the written ingredient quantities.
unsupportedRecipePolicy: There is no generic stock-photo fallback. Changed ingredient names or preparation methods invalidate managed imagery. Unknown recipes require review. User photos require explicit confirmation bound to the photo URL, recipe name, ingredient list and method. User-confirmed photos are never described as reviewed by the app.
sourceAuditExamples: The hummus recipe used a chocolate milkshake photograph.
Rice cake, cream puff and cheesecake recipes reused a chocolate layer cake photograph.
Several soups reused dry salad or unrelated meat stew photographs.
Different pasta recipes reused pesto bow-tie pasta.
Several old photographs included citrus absent from the recipes.
Some original PDF captions contradicted the pictured food.

atlases.prompt:
Create ONE production sprite atlas asset for a recipe-planner application. This is a recipe ILLUSTRATION atlas, not documentary photography. Required canvas: 2048 by 2048 pixels. EXACTLY 4 equal columns and 4 equal rows:16separate squaretiles, no gaps, no lines, no text, no numbers, no logos. Realistic editorial-food-photography style on a simplewarm ivorybackground. Each completeplate, bowl or glass remains in its own tile. Correct proteins, carbohydrate, preparation and listed sides. Only listed ingredients; no citrus or unlisted garnish. Recipe order and complete source ingredients/methods follow.

Row1 column1: Overnight Oats with Berries. Ingredients: 0.5 cup rolled oats; 0.75 cup almond milk; 1 tbsp chia seeds; 0.5 cup mixed berries; 1 tsp honey. Method: Combine oats, milk, chia seeds and honey in a jar. Refrigerate overnight for at least four hours. Top with berries before serving.

Row1 column2: Veggie Egg Scramble. Ingredients: 3  egg; 0.5 cup spinach; 0.25 cup bell pepper; 0.25 cup onion; 1 tsp olive oil. Method: Sauté onion and pepper in olive oil for three minutes. Add spinach until wilted. Add beaten eggs and scramble until just set.

Row1 column3: Greek Yogurt Parfait. Ingredients: 1 cup greek yogurt; 0.25 cup granola; 0.5 cup mixed berries; 1 tsp honey. Method: Layer yogurt, granola and berries in a glass. Drizzle with honey.

Row1 column4: Quinoa Chickpea Salad. Ingredients: 0.75 cup quinoa; 1 can chickpeas; 1 cup cucumber; 1 cup cherry tomatoes; 2 tbsp olive oil; 1 tbsp rice vinegar; 0.25 cup feta cheese. Method: Cook quinoa and let it cool. Chop cucumber and halve tomatoes. Toss everything with olive oil and rice vinegar.

Row2 column1: Grilled Chicken Wrap. Ingredients: 150 g chicken breast; 1 pc whole-wheat tortilla; 0.5 cup lettuce; 0.25 cup tomato; 2 tbsp greek yogurt; 1 tsp olive oil. Method: Season and grill chicken for five to six minutes per side, then slice. Spread yogurt on the tortilla and add lettuce, tomato and chicken. Roll tightly and halve.

Row2 column2: Hearty Lentil Soup. Ingredients: 1 cup red lentils; 1 pc carrot; 1 pc celery stalk; 0.5 cup onion; 2 clove garlic; 4 cup vegetable broth; 1 tbsp olive oil; 1 tsp cumin. Method: Sauté onion, carrot, celery and garlic in oil. Add lentils, cumin and broth, then simmer for 25 minutes. Season and serve.

Row2 column3: Baked Salmon & Roasted Veggies. Ingredients: 180 g salmon fillet; 1 cup broccoli; 1 pc zucchini; 1 cup sweet potato; 2 tbsp olive oil; 1 tbsp rice vinegar. Method: Toss vegetables with oil and roast at 200°C for 15 minutes. Add salmon, drizzle rice vinegar over it, and bake for 12 to 14 minutes more.

Row2 column4: Tofu Stir-Fry with Brown Rice. Ingredients: 200 g firm tofu; 0.75 cup brown rice; 1 cup broccoli; 0.5 cup bell pepper; 2 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp sesame oil; 1 clove garlic; 1 tsp ginger. Method: Cook brown rice. Pan-fry cubed tofu until golden. Stir-fry vegetables with garlic and ginger, then add tofu and soy sauce. Serve over rice.

Row3 column1: Turkey & Bean Chili. Ingredients: 300 g ground turkey; 1 can kidney beans; 1 can diced tomatoes; 0.5 cup onion; 2 clove garlic; 1 tbsp chili powder; 1 tsp cumin; 1 tbsp olive oil. Method: Brown turkey with onion and garlic in oil. Add spices, beans and tomatoes. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes.

Row3 column2: Zucchini Noodles with Pesto. Ingredients: 2 pc zucchini; 3 tbsp pesto; 1 cup cherry tomatoes; 2 tbsp parmesan; 1 tbsp pine nuts; 1 tsp olive oil. Method: Spiralize zucchini into noodles. Sauté for two minutes in olive oil. Toss with pesto and tomatoes, then top with parmesan and pine nuts.

Row3 column3: Hummus & Veggie Sticks. Ingredients: 0.33 cup homemade hummus (chickpeas, tahini, garlic, rice vinegar, water); 1 pc carrot; 1 pc celery stalk; 0.5 cup bell pepper. Method: Cut vegetables into sticks. Blend cooked chickpeas, tahini, garlic, rice vinegar and water into a plain hummus; serve with the vegetables.

Row3 column4: Apple with Peanut Butter. Ingredients: 1 pc apple; 2 tbsp peanut butter. Method: Slice the apple. Serve with peanut butter for dipping.

Row4 column1: Healthy Carbonara. Ingredients: 60 g whole-wheat spaghetti; 1  egg; 0.25 cup plain Greek yogurt; 1 cup button mushrooms; 1 cup baby spinach; 0.25 cup green peas; 2 tbsp grated parmesan; 1 tsp olive oil; 1 clove garlic; 0.25 tsp black pepper. Method: Cook the whole-wheat spaghetti until al dente. Reserve half a cup of pasta water, then drain. Whisk the egg, Greek yogurt, parmesan and black pepper until smooth. Use a pasteurized egg when available. Heat olive oil in a pan. Sauté garlic and mushrooms for four to five minutes, then add peas and spinach until wilted. Add the drained spaghetti, toss, then remove the pan from the heat. Whisk two tablespoons of hot pasta water into the egg mixture. Pour it over the pasta while tossing continuously. Return to very low heat and toss for one to two minutes until the sauce is steaming and coats the pasta. Do not boil; add pasta water as needed.

Row4 column2: Healthy Hot Pancakes. Ingredients: 0.5 cup rolled oats; 0.5 pc ripe banana; 1  egg; 0.25 cup low-fat milk; 0.5 tsp baking powder; 0.25 tsp cinnamon; 1 tsp olive oil; 0.25 cup mixed berries. Method: Blend the rolled oats into a fine flour. Mash the banana, then whisk it with the egg and low-fat milk. Stir in the oat flour, baking powder and cinnamon. Rest the batter for five minutes. Lightly coat a nonstick pan with olive oil and heat it over medium-low heat. Cook small pancakes for two to three minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Serve hot with mixed berries instead of syrup.

Row4 column3: Healthy Buko Coconut Bowl. Ingredients: 0.5 cup fresh buko meat; 0.5 cup unsweetened coconut water; 0.5 cup plain Greek yogurt; 1 tbsp chia seeds; 0.25 cup diced pineapple; 0.25 cup ice. Method: Chill the buko meat, coconut water and Greek yogurt before assembling. Slice the fresh buko meat into thin strips. Stir the Greek yogurt, coconut water and chia seeds together until creamy. Fold in the buko strips and diced pineapple. Serve immediately over ice, or chill for 10 minutes to let the chia seeds thicken the bowl.

Row4 column4: Healthy Pancit Bihon. Ingredients: 60 g bihon noodles; 80 g skinless chicken breast; 1 cup cabbage; 0.5 cup carrot; 0.5 cup bell pepper; 0.5 cup snap peas; 1 tsp olive oil; 1 clove garlic; 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce; 1 cup unsalted chicken broth; 1 tbsp rice vinegar. Method: Soak the bihon noodles according to package directions, then drain. Slice the chicken and vegetables thinly so they cook quickly and evenly. Heat olive oil in a wide pan. Sauté garlic and chicken until the chicken is fully cooked. Add cabbage, carrot, bell pepper and snap peas. Stir-fry for three to four minutes so the vegetables stay crisp. Pour in the unsalted broth and low-sodium soy sauce, then add the noodles. Toss until the noodles absorb the liquid. Finish with rice vinegar and serve hot.

atlases.prompt:
Create ONE production food ILLUSTRATION sprite atlas, exact 4 columns by 4 rows of equal square cells, reading order left to right then top to bottom. Entire output square 2048x2048 pixels or greater, no gutters, gaps, borders, labels, letters, words, numerals, watermarks, or extra dishes. Consistent warm off-white background throughout, clean realistic editorial FOOD ILLUSTRATION style, not a camera photograph. Each cell shows a single complete dish, bowl, plate, pastry or drink centered fully within its cell with comfortable internal margin, viewed from a slight overhead angle, distinct and readily recognizable at thumbnail size. Nothing crosses cell boundaries. Exactly16 dishes in the specified arrangement. Render each dish according to its actual ingredient list and preparation below: match protein, carbohydrate, color, cooking method, and side vegetables, add no unlisted ingredient or garnish. Absolutely NO citrus of any kind, NO lemons/limes/oranges/calamansi, NO garnish or decorations not in that cell's ingredients. Do not swap recipes between cells. For fish show the specified species fillet, for poultry skinless cooked boneless breast meat, for whole-grain dishes use visibly brown whole-grain rice/grains/pasta. Do not add meat to vegetarian recipes. Do not render instructions or text. These Filipino vegetable dishes have exact distinct appearances: monggo is a mungbean stew, pinakbet is a colorful vegetable saute with crisp tofu cubes and pale adlai grains, kare-kare is a peanut-sauce vegetable stew, tinola is a clear ginger chicken soup. No shrimp paste, meat, mayonnaise or citrus on any tofu or vegetable dish.

CELL CONTENTS (numbers are directions only; never draw them):
ROW 1, COLUMN 1: Healthy Rice Cake. Ingredients: brown rice flour, baking powder, egg, unsweetened light coconut milk, honey, coconut oil, fresh buko meat, cinnamon. Preparation: Heat the oven to 180°C and lightly grease a small baking dish or four muffin cups with coconut oil. Whisk the brown rice flour, baking powder and cinnamon together in a bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg, light coconut milk and honey until smooth. Fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients just until combined, then stir in the sliced fresh buko meat. Pour into the prepared dish and bake for 24 to 28 minutes, until the center is set and the top is lightly golden. Cool for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm without additional syrup.

ROW 1, COLUMN 2: Healthy Chicken Adobo. Ingredients: skinless chicken breast, low-sodium soy sauce, cane vinegar, water, garlic, bay leaf, black pepper, olive oil, green beans, brown rice. Preparation: Marinate the chicken in low-sodium soy sauce, cane vinegar, garlic and black pepper for 10 minutes. Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat and brown the chicken on both sides. Pour in the marinade and water, then add the bay leaf. Cover and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74°C in the thickest part. Add the green beans for the final four to five minutes, then uncover and reduce the sauce until lightly thickened. Discard the bay leaf and serve the adobo with cooked brown rice.

ROW 1, COLUMN 3: Savory Oatmeal with Tofu & Pechay. Ingredients: rolled oats, firm tofu, pechay, tomato, olive oil, garlic, low-sodium soy sauce, turmeric, black pepper. Preparation: Cook the oats with one cup of water over medium-low heat until creamy, about five minutes. Pat the tofu dry, crumble it, and brown it in half of the olive oil for four to five minutes. Add the remaining oil, garlic, tomato and turmeric. Cook until the tomato softens. Fold in the pechay and low-sodium soy sauce, cooking just until the leaves wilt. Spoon the tofu and vegetables over the oats and finish with black pepper. Do not add sugar or salty toppings.

ROW 1, COLUMN 4: Cherry Chia Yogurt Oats. Ingredients: rolled oats, plain low-fat Greek yogurt, unsweetened tart cherries, chia seeds, ground flaxseed, cinnamon, water. Preparation: Stir the rolled oats, chia seeds, ground flaxseed and cinnamon together in a jar. Add the Greek yogurt and water, then mix until evenly combined. Fold in half of the unsweetened cherries. Cover and refrigerate for at least four hours or overnight. Top with the remaining cherries and serve without honey, syrup or sweetened granola.

ROW 2, COLUMN 1: Malunggay Egg-White Omelet & Kamote. Ingredients: egg white, egg, malunggay leaves, tomato, onion, olive oil, roasted sweet potato, black pepper. Preparation: Whisk the egg whites and whole egg with black pepper. Heat half of the olive oil in a nonstick pan and sauté the onion and tomato for three minutes. Add the malunggay leaves and cook until just wilted. Pour in the egg mixture and cook over low heat until set, folding once. Serve with the measured roasted sweet potato; skip ketchup and sweet sauces.

ROW 2, COLUMN 2: Monggo Malunggay Bowl. Ingredients: cooked mung beans, malunggay leaves, squash, tomato, onion, garlic, unsalted vegetable broth, olive oil, brown rice, black pepper. Preparation: Heat the olive oil and sauté the onion, garlic and tomato until softened. Add the squash and unsalted broth, then simmer until the squash is almost tender. Stir in the cooked mung beans and simmer for eight to ten minutes. Fold in the malunggay leaves for the final two minutes and season with black pepper. Serve with one-third cup cooked brown rice. Keep the dish meat-free and do not add bagoong or processed meat.

ROW 2, COLUMN 3: Tofu Pinakbet with Adlai. Ingredients: firm tofu, eggplant, okra, squash, sitaw, tomato, onion, canola oil, low-sodium soy sauce, cooked adlai. Preparation: Pat the tofu dry, cube it, and brown it in half of the canola oil. Set aside. Add the remaining oil, onion and tomato to the pan and cook until softened. Add the squash with a splash of water, cover, and cook for four minutes. Add the eggplant, okra and sitaw. Cook until tender-crisp, then return the tofu. Season with one teaspoon low-sodium soy sauce and serve over the measured adlai. This version intentionally omits bagoong.

ROW 2, COLUMN 4: Lean Chicken Tinola Bowl. Ingredients: skinless chicken breast, sayote, malunggay leaves, ginger, onion, garlic, unsalted chicken broth, olive oil, brown rice, rice vinegar. Preparation: Heat the olive oil and sauté the ginger, onion and garlic until fragrant. Add the chicken breast and cook until the outside is no longer pink. Pour in the unsalted broth and simmer gently for 12 minutes. Add the sayote and cook until tender, then fold in the malunggay leaves for two minutes. Check that the chicken reaches 74°C, finish with rice vinegar, and serve with one-third cup cooked brown rice.

ROW 3, COLUMN 1: Ginger Salmon with Okra & Barley. Ingredients: salmon fillet, cooked pearl barley, okra, broccoli, olive oil, rice vinegar, ginger, black pepper. Preparation: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a tray with parchment. Arrange the salmon, okra and broccoli on the tray. Brush with olive oil and season with ginger and black pepper. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes and reaches 63°C. Warm the cooked barley with a splash of water. Finish the salmon and vegetables with rice vinegar and serve with the measured barley. Keep the fish portion to 120 grams.

ROW 3, COLUMN 2: Tokwa Mushroom Sisig Lettuce Cups. Ingredients: firm tofu, button mushrooms, red bell pepper, red onion, rice vinegar, low-sodium soy sauce, olive oil, lettuce leaves, brown rice, black pepper. Preparation: Pat the tofu dry, crumble it, and brown it in a nonstick pan with half of the olive oil. Add the remaining oil and mushrooms, cooking until their moisture evaporates. Stir in the bell pepper and red onion and cook for two minutes so they retain some crunch. Remove from heat and mix in the rice vinegar, low-sodium soy sauce and black pepper. Spoon into lettuce leaves and serve with one-third cup cooked brown rice. Do not add mayonnaise or processed meat.

ROW 3, COLUMN 3: Vegetable Kare-Kare with Brown Rice. Ingredients: firm tofu, eggplant, sitaw, pechay, squash, unsweetened peanut butter, brown rice flour, canola oil, garlic, onion, unsalted vegetable broth, brown rice. Preparation: Brown the cubed tofu in half of the canola oil and set aside. Sauté the garlic and onion in the remaining oil, then add the squash and unsalted broth. Whisk the peanut butter and brown rice flour with a little warm broth, then stir the mixture into the pot. Add the eggplant and sitaw and simmer until tender; return the tofu and fold in the pechay. Serve with one-third cup cooked brown rice. Skip bagoong to keep sodium lower.

ROW 3, COLUMN 4: Apple Oat-Bran Yogurt Cup. Ingredients: apple, plain low-fat Greek yogurt, oat bran, ground flaxseed, cinnamon. Preparation: Dice the apple, keeping the peel for added fiber. Spoon the plain low-fat Greek yogurt into a bowl. Stir in the oat bran and ground flaxseed. Top with the apple and cinnamon and serve immediately without honey or syrup.

ROW 4, COLUMN 1: Green Papaya Cucumber Salad. Ingredients: shredded green papaya, cucumber, tomato, rice vinegar, unsalted roasted peanuts, olive oil, black pepper. Preparation: Combine the shredded green papaya, cucumber and tomato in a bowl. Whisk the rice vinegar, olive oil and black pepper. Toss the vegetables with the dressing and let them stand for five minutes. Top with unsalted roasted peanuts and serve chilled. Do not add sugar, fish sauce or bagoong.

ROW 4, COLUMN 2: Soy Cacao Chia Pudding. Ingredients: unsweetened soy milk, chia seeds, unsweetened cocoa powder, mixed berries, cinnamon, vanilla extract. Preparation: Whisk the soy milk, chia seeds, cocoa powder, cinnamon and vanilla until no cocoa lumps remain. Rest for five minutes, whisk again, then cover. Refrigerate for at least four hours or overnight. Stir before serving and top with the mixed berries. Keep it unsweetened; do not add syrup or condensed milk.

ROW 4, COLUMN 3: Garlic-Herb Grilled Chicken Bowl. Ingredients: skinless chicken breast, cooked tri-color quinoa, broccoli, cherry tomatoes, red onion, rice vinegar, apple cider vinegar, olive oil, garlic, fresh parsley, dried oregano, black pepper. Preparation: Combine the sliced red onion with the apple cider vinegar and one tablespoon of water. Set aside for at least 15 minutes to quick-pickle without added sugar. Coat the chicken with one tablespoon rice vinegar, half of the olive oil, oregano and black pepper. Grill over medium-high heat for five to six minutes per side, until the center reaches 74°C, then rest and slice. Roast the broccoli and cherry tomatoes at 210°C with a light coating of the remaining oil for 12 to 15 minutes. Whisk the remaining rice vinegar with the minced garlic, parsley and any remaining olive oil to make the garlic-herb vinaigrette. Add the cooked tri-color quinoa to a bowl, then arrange the roasted vegetables, drained pickled onion and sliced charred chicken on top. Drizzle with the garlic-herb vinaigrette. Brown rice may replace the quinoa in the same measured portion.

ROW 4, COLUMN 4: Miso Glazed Salmon Fillet. Ingredients: salmon fillet, cooked brown rice, shelled edamame, shredded purple cabbage, cucumber, white miso paste, low-sodium soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, sesame seeds. Preparation: Whisk the white miso, low-sodium soy sauce, half of the rice vinegar, sesame oil and grated ginger into a smooth sesame-ginger glaze. Pat the salmon dry and brush it with half of the glaze. Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon skin-side down for four to five minutes, turn, add the remaining glaze, and cook until the center reaches 63°C. Steam the shelled edamame until hot. Use a vegetable peeler to cut the cucumber into ribbons. Season the warm brown rice with the remaining rice vinegar, add it to a bowl, and arrange the edamame, shredded purple cabbage and cucumber ribbons around it. Place the pan-roasted salmon fillet on top, spoon over the warm glaze, and finish with sesame seeds.

Row 1 column 1: Mediterranean Falafel & Egg Bowl. Ingredients: 0.75 cup cooked chickpeas; 0.25 cup fresh parsley; 1 clove garlic; 0.5 tsp ground cumin; 1 tsp olive oil; 2  egg; 2 tbsp homemade hummus (chickpeas, tahini, garlic, rice vinegar, water); 2 cup mixed greens; 4 pc kalamata olives; 0.5 cup cucumber; 1 tbsp tahini; 1 tbsp rice vinegar; 0.25 tsp black pepper. Preparation: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a small baking tray. Pulse the chickpeas, parsley, garlic, cumin and black pepper until crumbly. Shape into three small patties, brush with olive oil, and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning halfway. Lower the eggs into gently boiling water for seven minutes, then transfer them to ice water. Peel and halve once cool enough to handle. Finely grate half of the cucumber and whisk it with the tahini, rice vinegar and one to two tablespoons of water until pourable. Slice the remaining cucumber. Fill a bowl with the mixed greens and sliced cucumber, then add the baked falafel patties, soft-boiled eggs, homemade hummus (blend chickpeas, tahini, garlic, rice vinegar and water) and kalamata olives. Drizzle with the cucumber-tahini dressing and serve immediately.

Row 1 column 2: Bangus Sisig. Ingredients: 120 g boneless bangus fillet; 0.33 cup cooked brown rice; 0.25 cup red onion; 0.5 cup red bell pepper; 1 clove garlic; 1 pc green chili; 1 tbsp rice vinegar; 1 tsp olive oil; 2 pc lettuce leaves; 0.25 tsp black pepper. Preparation: Check the bangus fillet for pin bones, pat dry, and season with black pepper. Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat with half the olive oil. Cook the bangus for about five to seven minutes per side, until the thickest part reaches 63°C. Remove from the pan and flake into bite-sized pieces, checking again for bones. Add the remaining oil, garlic, red onion, bell pepper and sliced green chili to the pan. Cook for two to three minutes until fragrant but still crisp. Return the flaked bangus to the pan and toss briefly until the edges brown. Turn off the heat and stir in the rice vinegar. Serve the sisig on the lettuce leaves with one-third cup cooked brown rice. Skip mayonnaise and salty seasoning; add fresh herbs to taste.

Row 1 column 3: Garlic yogurt chicken grain bowl. Ingredients: 120 g cooked grilled chicken; 150 g cooked brown rice; 0.5 cup cucumber; 1 cup lettuce; 0.25 cup carrots; 1 tsp rice vinegar; 60 g plain yogurt; 1 clove garlic; 10 g Nutrilite All Plant Protein Powder. Preparation: Grill chicken to 74°C and rest before slicing. Plate brown rice, washed vegetables and chicken. Whisk 10 g plant protein into cold yogurt with garlic and rice vinegar; drizzle before serving.
